name: Deferred Splatting with Temporal Coherency and Bi-Bi-1 Visibility Pass
definition: A rendering algorithm that uses deferred splatting to render point-based models efficiently. It separates visibility determination from color accumulation, using temporal coherency to accelerate the visibility pass and a secondary visibility pass (Bi - Bi-1) to fix artifacts caused by hidden points becoming visible.
summary: This algorithm reduces rendering costs by performing expensive splatting only on visible surfels, using temporal coherency and a secondary pass to fix artifacts from hidden points becoming visible.
